messages:
maria: Heads up — canary for v2.3.1 is showing a p99 regression on long-seq jobs in eu-west. Dashboard: p99 went from ~220ms -> ~270ms over the last 10m. Can we pause the canary and collect profiles before the rollout continues?

perf-bot: automated alert — canary:v2.3.1 | region=eu-west | p99=270ms (+22%) | error_rate=0.02% | link=https://perf.redwood.internal/canary/2023456789 :warning:

alex: copy. can we narrow to model variants? Is this happening on quantized lanes only or across all kernels?

maria: initial look shows spike primarily on the int8-llama-13b quantized variant. float16 lanes look flat.

sam: ok — likely kernel/quantization perf. i can run a quick sampling profile on one of the canary hosts. need sudo on the instance though. who has access?

todd: i can open a short window. recommendation: dont fully rollback yet. hold traffic -> reduce to 10% and set canary to 'held' so it won't auto-promote. that gives us time to profile.

maria: agreed. canary hold + profiles. alex, sam — can you coordinate and get a flamegraph? if we reproduce on a host, grab both perf and nvprof if GPU visible. target: root-cause within 45m.

alex: i'll repro and collect `perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60` + `python -m pyflame` for the worker, then upload flamegraph to /tmp/canary-profiles.

sam: i'll also capture `nvprof --analysis-metrics -o nvprof.cua` on the worker that owns GPU0. sharing the exact instance in #eng-infra in 2m.

maria: ops — please run the hold command:
```
# temporarily reduce traffic and mark canary held
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/canaries/v2.3.1/state \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"state":"held","traffic_pct":10}'
```

perf-bot: action scheduled — set canary state to held, traffic 10% initiated by maria at 2023456810.

todd: noted. also adding rollback guard: if p99 stays >250ms AND error_rate >0.1% for 10m we auto-rollback. do we agree?

alex: +1 to p99>250ms sustained 10m OR error_rate>0.1% for 5m. that covers perf-only vs reliability.

sam: sounds good. i'll prioritize bisecting kernel flags after profiling. if we find a malloc/kern path, we can flip the kernel variant.

maria: owner assignments: alex=collect perf & flamegraphs, sam=GPU traces and kernel bisect, todd=hold & rollback automation, i'll coordinate with product for release timing. target update at +30m (2023456869).

todd: i've queued the rollback-watch rule: `if (p99>250 && p99_delta>20%) || (error_rate>0.1%) then rollback`. will alert #incidents and do a staged rollback to previous model variant.

alex: uploading initial flamegraph: https://artifacts.redwood/internal/flamegraphs/2023456789/alex-1.svg — early signal: hotspots in aten::embedding_backward and cpu->gpu memcpy path.

sam: nvprof shows increased memcpy and some kernel grid divergence on int8 quant path. collecting a longer trace now.

maria: thanks. if either of you call rollback, do it with the staged plan: 50% -> 0% over 5m so clients can failover. no full account-wide mass rollback unless we see error spikes.

perf-bot: scheduled check at 2023456869 for status update.

maria: closing loop — pause promotion, collecting profiles. will reconvene at status tick. :thumbsup:
